findings.title: parseQuantity does not validate input or radix, allowing NaN to reach cart totals
findings.problem: parseQuantity(text) calls parseInt(text) with no explicit radix and no check that the result is a valid, non-negative integer. parseInt silently truncates trailing non-numeric characters (e.g. "2abc" -> 2) and returns NaN for non-numeric input (e.g. "" or "abc") without throwing. Any NaN or unexpected value returned here can propagate into subtotal(), where it is multiplied against priceCents, corrupting the cart total.
findings.recommendedFix: Use Number.parseInt(text, 10) with an explicit radix, validate the result with Number.isInteger and a minimum bound (e.g. >= 0 or >= 1), and throw or return a clear error/sentinel for invalid input rather than silently returning NaN or a truncated number.
